openai.reasoning: The respondent never commits to pressing either button and instead argues that the best choice depends on beliefs about what the majority will do; they also discuss rationality without selecting a personal vote, so there is no rule-mechanics error but no dominant-strategy application is demonstrated.

gemini.reasoning: The respondent provides a comprehensive game-theoretic analysis of the dilemma, correctly identifying it as a coordination game with two Nash equilibria. They explicitly state that there is no dominant strategy in the sense of a single button that is always safer, but they fail to recognize that RED is the dominant strategy because they incorrectly believe that red-pressers die if the majority presses blue (the prompt states everyone survives if the majority presses blue). Because they believe red-pressers die when blue wins, they incorrectly conclude that the choice depends entirely on predicting the majority, rather than recognizing that RED is safer regardless of the outcome.
